controls_available: Difficulty 5 generates 15 visible heptagonal faces, an exact eight-twist scramble, and a ten-twist move budget.
In simplified mode, click a visible heptagon to center it; this changes the Mobius view and focused face but not sticker state.
Use the visible counter-clockwise or clockwise proxy button to synchronously twist the centered face. Each accepted twist mutates the sticker state and consumes one move.
RESET SCRAMBLE synchronously restores the initial puzzle. CERTIFY submits the current state and is administrative; no full-mode drag or keyboard mechanic is active.
autonomous_processes: None: after render and between agent actions, the view, sticker state, focused face, and twist count remain unchanged; the source has no task timer, physics, animation loop, decay, or random state update.

An outcome-affecting twist remains available while the puzzle is unsubmitted and under the ten-twist budget, but waiting does not change its target, effectiveness, or availability. Certification/network response does not create an autonomous puzzle phase.

clause_i.reason: For the grouped twist mode, different generated scrambles can have the same own action history and task time but require different next face and direction choices. Thus an observation-free q using only I_t cannot be optimal for every still-solvable history, while the current screenshot exposes the visible sticker arrangement needed to choose the twist.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded current screenshot is sufficient for the static puzzle: it shows the colored sectors and face geometry, and the next optimal twist can be selected from that visible state together with the prior focus/action history. No past frame or autonomous trajectory is required.

clause_iii.reason: There is no H_t^tau with autonomous task-state change for any positive delay. The browser changes model.current only inside synchronous focus, twist, reset, or submission handlers; CSS is static and has no animation/keyframe path. Waiting only advances the external play-time allowance, which the frozen definition excludes, and does not strictly reduce the value or availability of a twist. Therefore no valid positive Delta and common visible autonomous process exists.

common_visible_process: None. The colored puzzle is stationary between actions; visible focus, twist, and reset transitions are caused by agent input. Consequently no single visible autonomous process can witness all three clauses.

pre_run.reason: The source provides no autonomous outcome phase: every successful instance requires outcome-affecting twist actions after the static challenge is shown. Certification is administrative only, so no generated instance qualifies as a pre-run solution under the stated rule. No numeric rate is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is very_hard with face_count 15, scramble_length 8, and move_budget 10; simplified interaction uses a visible heptagon click plus explicit counter-clockwise/clockwise buttons; observation_window_ms is 0 and frames_per_observation is 1.
The runner repeats the zero-millisecond observation window, one frame, 180-second play allowance, and synchronous execution for this environment.

The generator reads the selected control condition once, constructs a seeded initial sticker state and exact-depth scramble, and emits static puzzle geometry, state, cycles, and move budget; it has no autonomous update path.
applyTwist validates the aperture, synchronously computes and records the permutation, increments twists, assigns model.current, redraws, and returns; no delay or autonomous continuation is involved.
Simplified clicks only center a face and update the view/focus; full-mode dragging is disabled by the interaction guard; reset is also a synchronous event handler.

The simplified proxy buttons call applyTwist only on click, while CERTIFY serializes the current state for grading; render installs event listeners and performs one initial draw without a timer or animation loop.
The complete stylesheet contains static layout, appearance, hover, cursor, and status rules, with no animation or keyframe declaration that could autonomously change the puzzle.
The grader selects proxy_buttons for simplified interaction and replays focus/twist events against the sticker state, checking the solved monochrome outcome and budget without task-time evolution.
The authoritative verifier independently replays the same visible event transcript and checks final state, counts, and solved condition; it has no clock- or delay-dependent criterion.

The screenshot/UI solver centers each target face and presses the simplified direction button, waiting only for synchronous event counters before continuing; it does not rely on an evolving task state.
The shared helper used by the task verifier only copies and parses the exported result, then removes its temporary file; it does not advance or mutate puzzle state.

The frozen definition requires autonomous visible task-state change that strictly degrades an action opportunity within a positive Delta, and separately defines the pre-run threshold while excluding mere deadline passage.
